# Distance to original: the gap catalogue

<!-- Generated by jobol-audit compare-gaps from the compare reports and compare-catalogue.json; do not edit by hand. -->

This catalogue compares the original Java of four estates with the modern Java that MlCpu.Modernize generated from the J3S COBOL of that Java (original Java → J3S → COBOL → MlCpu.Modernize → modern Java). The original Java is the held-out answer key: the generator never sees it, and nothing here changes a generator. It is measurement and design input for generic generator rules, which another session specifies.

Each estate's measurements are in `compare/<estate>/compare-report.md` (and `.json`): type alignment, API, name and signature fidelity, idioms, structure, the top 20 types by distance, and every gap instance. `jobol-audit compare-gaps` groups the instances into the patterns below. The patterns, their classes and their hypotheses come from `compare-catalogue.json`; the counts and examples come from the reports. Regenerate with `tools/jobol-auditor/compare-estates.sh` and do not edit this file by hand.

Read the counts with three facts in mind.

1. **J3S compiles only what the estate's jobs reach.** Most of the original API that is missing from modern Java was never compiled to COBOL, so no generator could restore it. The `--cobol` option reads the J3S CLASS headers and FRAME comments. Methods with no frame are reported as `METHOD.UNREACHED_*` (pattern G27), not as losses. "Reached" API preservation is the generator's own score: 93.3% for joda-money, 79.4% for kontor-zins, 90.9% for loanamorti and 83.7% for fineract-xl. Every method J3S reached is present in modern Java: `METHOD.MISSING_*` and `OVERLOAD.COLLAPSED` are zero in all four estates (G29). The overloads that looked collapsed were overloads J3S never compiled.
2. **Idioms are compared over the comparable part.** On the original side, idiom and type-use counts leave out methods with no modern counterpart. The reports show both columns ("original, all" and "original").
3. **Pipeline infrastructure is not a gap.** The generated job, platform, record and strangler layers have no original. They are classified by the auditor's lanes (`default-jobol.json`: `**/batch/platform/**`, `**/record/**`, `**/strangler/**` and others are compat) and by `compareInfrastructureGlobs` (`**/batch/**`, the application layer). That covers 36, 37, 37 and 50 modern-only types. They are counted, and are not listed as gaps.

Hypotheses name the COBOL-side evidence a rule could use. The evidence types are these. FRAME comments (`* FRAME OF M0515-LSPAR-NEW LoanScheduleParams.<init>(int, int, ..., Money>, ...)`) give full method names and parameter types by their last dotted segment, so a generic parameter keeps only its last type argument (`Money>`). ENTRY and SRC comments give externally called functions and the original source line spans. CLASS headers give the compiled classes. Data names are cut (frame locals and parameters keep 12 characters, `F0516-L-LOAN-TERM-IN`). There are PICTURE sizes, EVALUATE shapes, the exception class-id tables (`JO-SIMPLE-NAME`), and the identifiers the generated estate already spells out.

### G01: Truncated identifiers the estate can complete

Class **a**. A field, parameter, local, method or constant whose modern spelling is the original with its tail cut (`totalFeeChargesChar` for `totalFeeChargesCharged`, `termInMont`). Exactly one identifier elsewhere in the modern estate extends the cut name and it is the original (unique-correct), or several do and the original is one of them (ambiguous-correct). Cut lengths cluster at 10–11 characters (frame locals and parameters) and spread over 14–24 for fields (the 30-character COBOL name, less the prefix).

Counts: joda-money 3, kontor-zins 1, loanamorti 3, fineract-xl 201 (total 208). Gap codes: `NAME.TRUNCATED.AMBIGUOUS_CORRECT` 92, `NAME.TRUNCATED.UNIQUE_CORRECT` 109, `NAME.TRUNCATED_NUMBERED.AMBIGUOUS_CORRECT` 7.

| Estate | Type | Member | Original | Modern | Detail |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| joda-money | `CurrencyUnit` | registerCurrency(String,int,int,List,boolean) | countryCodes | countryCode | param, completion ambiguous-correct |
| joda-money | `BigMoney` | getCurrencyUnit() | getCurrencyUnit | getCurrency | method, completion unique-correct |
| joda-money | `CurrencyUnit` | registerCurrency(String,int,int,boolean) | countryCodes | countryCode | local, completion ambiguous-correct |
| kontor-zins | `Schedule` | validate() | totalPrincipal | totalPrinci | local, completion unique-correct |
| loanamorti | `LoanAmortization.LoanAmortizationBuilder` | overPaymentAmount(BigDecimal) | overPaymentAmount | overPayment | param, completion unique-correct |
| loanamorti | `MonthlyPayment.MonthlyPaymentBuilder` | debtPaymentAmount(BigDecimal) | debtPaymentAmount | debtPayment | param, completion unique-correct |
| loanamorti | `MonthlyPayment.MonthlyPaymentBuilder` | loanBalanceAmount(BigDecimal) | loanBalanceAmount | loanBalance | param, completion unique-correct |
| fineract-xl | `AbstractPlatformDomainRuleException` | &lt;init&gt;(String,String,Object[]) | defaultUserMessage | defaultUser | param, completion ambiguous-correct |
| fineract-xl | `AbstractPlatformException` | &lt;init&gt;(String,String,Object[]) | defaultUserMessage | defaultUser | param, completion ambiguous-correct |
| fineract-xl | `CurrencyData` | &lt;init&gt;(String,String,int,Integer,String,String) | inMultiplesOf | inMultiples | param, completion ambiguous-correct |

**COBOL-side evidence.** The full spelling survives elsewhere in the COBOL-derived estate: FRAME comments give full method names (`addTotalFeeChargesCharged`), getter and setter names give property names, and assignment `this.loanTermInDays = loanTermIn` links a cut parameter to a full field.

**Generic rule hypothesis.** Complete a cut name to the identifier it flows to or from: a parameter stored into a field takes the field's name, a field returned by a getter takes the property name, and an argument passed to a parameter takes the parameter's name. Only when no data-flow link exists, take the unique estate identifier the cut name is a prefix of. With several candidates, decide only by data flow, never by prefix length.

**Generic rule hypothesis.** Prefix completion with a lexicon (English and banking words): external knowledge, for example a dictionary or a language model limited to completions of the cut stem that are type-compatible. Never apply estate-prefix completion when it is unique-wrong: in fineract-xl it would be wrong 98+21 times. When unsure, keep the cut name. Completing both names of a collision removes the counter.

Class **a**. Word-by-word abbreviations: enum constants `CAP_INC` (CAPITALIZED_INCOME), `INT_RATE_CHANGE`, `PRIN_GRACE_LIFTED`, `DISB_DATE`, and fields `downPaymentPct` and `disbursedAmountPctF` (`disbursedAmountPercentageForDownPayment`). Most are words the generator's own abbreviation table (MODERNIZATION.md: CAP, INC, INT, PRIN, DISB...) already expands for fields and variables.

Counts: joda-money 1, kontor-zins 0, loanamorti 0, fineract-xl 18 (total 19). Gap codes: `NAME.ABBREVIATED` 19.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

### G04: Accessors invented in the wrong style

Class **a**. Where J3S never compiled an accessor, the generator invents one in the bean style even when the estate uses record-style accessors. kontor-zins `Schedule.installments()` becomes `getInstallments()`. Invented getters also carry cut field names (`getDisbursedAmountPctF`) or a doubled prefix (`isIsInterestRecalculationE`).

Counts: joda-money 0, kontor-zins 4, loanamorti 1, fineract-xl 15 (total 20). Gap codes: `METHOD.EXTRA_ACCESSOR` 9, `NAME.ACCESSOR_STYLE` 11.

| Estate | Type | Member | Original | Modern | Detail |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| kontor-zins | `Schedule` | installments() | installments | getInstallments | method |
| kontor-zins | `Schedule` | totalInterest() | totalInterest | getTotalInterest | method |
| kontor-zins | `Schedule` | totalPaid() | totalPaid | getTotalPaid | method |
| loanamorti | `LoanAmortization` | getEarlyPayments() | getEarlyPayments | earlyPayments | method |
| fineract-xl | `LoanApplicationTerms` | getVariationsDataWrappe() |  | Object getVariationsDataWrappe() | source public |
| fineract-xl | `ProgressiveLoanInterestScheduleModel` | getInstallmentAmountI() |  | Integer getInstallmentAmountI() | source public |
| fineract-xl | `LoanConfigurationDetails` | getInterestPaymentGrace() |  | Integer getInterestPaymentGrace() | source public |

**COBOL-side evidence.** The reached accessors' FRAME names give the estate's convention (`LoanTerms.principal()`, `Installment.month()`), and the field's full name (G01).

**Generic rule hypothesis.** Name invented accessors in the convention of the reached accessors of the same type, falling back to the estate's convention. Build the name from the completed field name. Never prefix `is` to a name that already starts with `is`.

### G07: Generic type arguments erased to Object

Class **a**. `Map<LocalDate,Money>` becomes `Map<Object,Object>`, `Set<Integer>` becomes `Set<Object>`, and `Supplier<? extends T>` becomes `Supplier<Object>`, in fields, parameters and returns. Generic arguments are dropped or changed (`List<T>` to `List<?>`). The modern code then casts at every use.

Counts: joda-money 0, kontor-zins 0, loanamorti 0, fineract-xl 27 (total 27). Gap codes: `TYPEREF.GENERIC_CHANGED` 6, `TYPEREF.GENERIC_DROPPED` 5, `TYPEREF.GENERIC_TO_OBJECT_KNOWN` 16.

| Estate | Type | Member | Original | Modern | Detail |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fineract-xl | `ProgressiveEMICalculator` | generateAdditionalRepaymentPeriodDueDates(ProgressiveLoanInterestScheduleModel,int,int,Function) | Function&lt;Long,LocalDate&gt; | Function&lt;Integer,LocalDate&gt; | param 4 |
| fineract-xl | `ProgressiveLoanInterestScheduleModel` | resolveRepaymentPeriodLengthGeneratorFunction(LocalDate) | Function&lt;Long,LocalDate&gt; | Function&lt;Integer,LocalDate&gt; | return |
| fineract-xl | `RepaymentPeriod` | calculatedDueInterestCalculation | Memo&lt;Money&gt; | Memo | field |

**COBOL-side evidence.** FRAME parameter lists keep the last type argument as a dangling `>` (`Money>` for `Map<LocalDate,Money>`). The modern code's own casts at get, put and iteration sites (`(LocalDate) k`) give the others.

**Generic rule hypothesis.** Type a collection by its frame `X>` token for the last argument and by the unique cast type at its use sites for the others. Remove the casts that become redundant.

### G08: Generic type parameters lost

Class **b**. Generic classes and methods become monomorphic: `Memo<T>` and `<T> generateInterestScheduleModel(List<T>, Function<T,LocalDate>, ...)` lose their type parameter.

Counts: joda-money 0, kontor-zins 0, loanamorti 0, fineract-xl 4 (total 4). Gap codes: `GENERICS.TYPE_PARAMETERS_LOST` 4.

| Estate | Type | Member | Original | Modern | Detail |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fineract-xl | `ProgressiveEMICalculator` | generateInterestScheduleModel(List,Function,Function,ILoanConfigurationDetails,Integer,MathContext) | &lt;T&gt; |  | method |
| fineract-xl | `Memo` |  | &lt;T&gt; |  | type |
| fineract-xl | `ProgressiveEMICalculator` | updateModel(ProgressiveLoanInterestScheduleModel,List,Function,Function) | &lt;T&gt; |  | method |

**COBOL-side evidence.** COBOL is monomorphic. Only the different cast types at each instantiation hint at a parameter.

**Generic rule hypothesis.** Introduce a type variable where one Object-typed slot is cast to different types at different call sites. This needs type inference beyond the COBOL evidence, so the type parameter's existence is an external judgement. Low frequency.

### G10: Known types become Object

Class **a**. Types the estate or the JDK declares are still typed `Object`, mostly fields that reached code only stores and never reads: `DisbursementData.note` and `linkAccountId` (String), `DateUtils.DEFAULT_DATE_FORMATTER` (DateTimeFormatter) and `BigMoney.PARSE_REGEX` (Pattern). Return types are affected too (`Money.zero(MonetaryCurrency)` returns `Object`).

Counts: joda-money 1, kontor-zins 0, loanamorti 0, fineract-xl 36 (total 37). Gap codes: `TYPEREF.TO_OBJECT_KNOWN` 37.

| Estate | Type | Member | Original | Modern | Detail |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| joda-money | `BigMoney` | PARSE_REGEX | Pattern | Object | field |
| fineract-xl | `AbstractPlatformException` | findThrowableCause(Object[]) | Throwable | Object | return |
| fineract-xl | `DateUtils` | DEFAULT_DATETIME_FORMAT | String | Object | field |
| fineract-xl | `Money` | of(MonetaryCurrency,BigDecimal) | Money | Object | return |

**COBOL-side evidence.** The constructor and setter FRAMEs that write the field carry the parameter type (`String`, `Money`). Static initialisers call a typed factory (`Pattern.compile`).

**Generic rule hypothesis.** Type a field by the frame types of the parameters assigned to it, or by the result type of its initialiser call. Type a method's return by the declared type of what it returns.

### G12: Primitive width, boxing and varargs drift

Class **a**. `short` becomes `int` (joda `CurrencyUnit.numericCode` and `decimalPlaces`), `Integer` becomes `int` (`periodNumber()`), and `Object...` becomes `Object[]` (MathUtil, AbstractPlatformException).

Counts: joda-money 4, kontor-zins 0, loanamorti 0, fineract-xl 6 (total 10). Gap codes: `TYPEREF.BOXING` 2, `TYPEREF.NUMERIC_CHANGED` 4, `TYPEREF.VARARGS_TO_ARRAY` 4.

| Estate | Type | Member | Original | Modern | Detail |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| joda-money | `CurrencyUnit` | &lt;init&gt;(String,short,short) | short | int | param 2 |
| joda-money | `CurrencyUnit` | &lt;init&gt;(String,short,short) | short | int | param 3 |
| joda-money | `CurrencyUnit` | decimalPlaces | short | int | field |

**COBOL-side evidence.** PIC S9(4) COMP against S9(9)/S9(10) COMP gives short against int. The `-C` null-flag item beside a numeric item gives a boxed type. Frames print varargs as arrays (`BigDecimal[]`), so restoring varargs needs the JDK convention (class b for that subcase).

**Generic rule hypothesis.** Map PICTURE sizes to the narrowest Java primitive J3S could have produced, and keep the boxed type where the item has a null flag. Make a trailing array parameter varargs when every call site builds a fresh array.

## Train/test split

Rules are derived from COBOL evidence. The original Java only scores them, so the split decides which estates' scores may be read while a rule is designed.

- **Train (derive and tune): fineract-xl and kontor-zins.** fineract-xl holds most instances of G01–G03, G07, G09–G11, G16, G17, G21 and G22 (67 types, 673 truncated names, generics, Lombok, streams). kontor-zins is the only estate with original records (G19) and the record-style accessor case (G04).
- **Test (validate once a rule set is frozen; read their reports only then): joda-money and loanamorti.** joda-money is a library by another author with a different naming style. It tests G01/G02 transfer, G12 (short), G14 (Comparable, Serializable), G15 (BigMoneyProvider, exception superclasses), G20 and G22 (public API narrowing matters in a library). loanamorti tests G11 (factories returning the implementation), G15 (LoanAmortizationCalculator, RepeatableEarlyPayment), G16 (streams) and G20.
- **Patterns with fewer than five training instances** (G05, G08, G12, G14, G19): use leave-one-estate-out over the four estates instead, and report each fold.
- **Generalisation check for class (a) rules:** run them on an estate with no original Java (carddemo). There, the JOBOL audit index and the GN4 strangler SHADOW equivalence must not regress. A rule that needs the original to fire is class (b), not (a).
- **Success measure:** on the test estates, the pattern's count falls and reached API, signature and name fidelity rise, with JOBOL audit and SHADOW equivalence unchanged. Track `NAME.TRUNCATED.UNIQUE_WRONG` separately: a completion rule that raises it is wrong even if name fidelity rises.

## Method

- **Scope.** With `--cobol`, the original side is the classes in J3S CLASS headers plus the types the modern estate names (by fully qualified name, or by a unique simple name for moved types). Nested types follow their outer type. Methods are reached when a FRAME comment names the owner's simple name, the method name and the parameter types (by last dotted segment; a dangling `X>` matches a generic parameter whose last argument is X; varargs match arrays).
- **Alignment.** Types align by fully qualified name, then by unique simple name (moved), then nested by unique simple name (relocated). Methods align by name and erased parameter types, then by name and arity, then by the remaining overloads in order. Names only on the original side align with a damaged modern name (truncated, abbreviated or accessor-style) of the same arity. Fields, parameters, locals and constants align exactly first, then by damaged form (preferring the same type and the longest shared prefix, with no guess on a tie), then as the single remaining name of an erased type.
- **Name classes** (Names.java): exact; case (the same words); truncated (a strict prefix, at least two characters); abbreviated (each word a prefix or an ordered letter subset of the original word); accessor-style (x() against getX()); truncated+numbered (a cut stem plus a counter); numbered (a counter or temporary name); renamed. For truncated names, "completion" says whether the modern estate's other identifiers would complete the stem: unique-correct, unique-wrong, ambiguous-correct, ambiguous-wrong or none.
- **Lombok.** No delombok run was available. The original side synthesises the members Lombok would generate (getters, setters, constructors, builder(), equals, hashCode, canEqual and toString) with origin `lombok`. A modern nested `XBuilder` class of an original `@Builder` type is classed as Lombok expansion.
- **Distance** per matched type is a sum of penalties: kind changed 5; type visibility 2; type modifier 1; supertype lost 3, added 1; reached API method missing 3, other reached method missing 2; extra method 1 (0.5 if private); changed parameter or return types 2; member visibility or static 1; field missing 2, extra 0.5, type changed 1, flag 0.5; enum constant missing 2, extra 1; field or method name not exact 1; parameter or local name not exact 0.25; reached builder lost 3; and per idiom unit lost 0.5, capped at 10 per family. Unreached methods cost nothing. "Per member" divides by the original's member count.
- **Determinism.** There is no clock, inputs are visited in sorted order, and all output lists are sorted. Two runs give identical bytes (CompareTest.compareIsDeterministic).
